subject: Patch dependency vulnerabilities and harden responses
body:
Production dependencies go from 6 advisories to none:
- express 4.21.2 -> 4.22.3, which carries path-to-regexp 0.1.13 (ReDoS via
  multiple route parameters, high) and qs 6.16.2 (several DoS paths).
- compression 1.7.5 -> 1.8.2, taking on-headers past 1.1.0 (response
  header manipulation, plus a memory leak on premature response close).
- postcss -> 8.5.33 (XSS via unescaped </style>, and arbitrary file read
  through an attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL).

The deploy repo's package.json is pinned to the same minimums. Production
installs from THAT manifest, so patching only this one would have changed
nothing on the live service.

Vite/esbuild is left at 5.x. The advisory is the dev server answering
cross-origin requests; it never runs in production, and the fix is vite 8,
which @vitejs/plugin-react does not support - npm refuses the install.
Worth revisiting when the plugin catches up.

Hardening:
- Permissions-Policy denies camera, microphone, geolocation, payment and
  the rest. Helmet does not set it and nothing here needs any of them.
- KYC documents are customer-supplied files served from our own origin,
  which is the usual way to get script running against a reviewer's
  session. They now carry a sandbox CSP that denies every source including
  scripts, X-Frame-Options DENY, and a filename stripped of quotes,
  backslashes and newlines so the Content-Disposition header cannot be
  split.

Checked and found clean: no SQL is built from user input (the one
interpolated fragment is chosen from a typed union), no secrets in any
tracked file or in git history, and session cookies are HttpOnly, Secure
and SameSite=Lax.

Verified: 99 checks still pass against the live database.
